answer: Each identity may claim one cedar lot: it locks a 60-credit bond and posts a jade-sealed claim on the public board naming its lot and work plan. Lots are finite, so the claim fee rises as lots go: first pays 40, kth pays 40 plus 25 per earlier claim, and the thousandth pays 25015. 1000 fakes lock 60000 and pay 12527500 in fees, each lot taking one key. A hollow-claim ring fails: a claim with no delivered work is opened by the lot inspector, its bond burns, and its key is barred from the next epoch. An honest agent pays 100 once and keeps its bond when its work is delivered.
